title: Space Comes in Three Words
hook: Astronauts can't go to the universe. Why?
summary: An astronaut can't go to the universe. They're already inside it.

text: English has three words for outer space.
space, universe, cosmos.

panels.text: Don't all three just mean outer space?

text: Astronauts go out into space.
It comes from Latin spatium, meaning room or extent.
That's why a parking spot is a parking space too.

panels.text: A parking lot and outer space are the same word?

text: Every dot in this photo is a galaxy, not a star.
Galaxies, light, time, you and me.
Add up everything that exists and you get the universe.
In Latin it means turned into one.

panels.mean: the universe as an ordered whole

text: The Greek word kosmos meant order.
It also meant decoration and adornment.
See the universe as one well-arranged world and you call it the cosmos.
Cosmetic comes from the same root.
It means to put a face in order.
The cosmos and makeup are relatives.
To sum up:
astronauts go to space,
scientists measure the universe,
and poets sing of the cosmos.
So an astronaut can't go to the universe.
They're already inside it.

panels.text: And the Chinese characters, 宇宙?

text: The ancient Chinese book Huainanzi says:
all directions and up and down are called 宇,
and the span from past to present is called 宙.
From the start, the word joined space and time.
